key_insight: A physics-informed neural network is used to learn corrections to a simple k-ε-b turbulence closure, improving Rayleigh-Taylor mixing predictions during the transition to turbulence.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a more accurate and interpretable RANS-based closure for early-stage mixing-layer growth, which is important for predictive simulations in buoyancy-driven flows.
method: Embed the k-ε-b model inside a surrogate PINN.
Calibrate model coefficients and identify missing-physics correction terms from data.
Re-express learned corrections as explicit analytical modifications using state variables and flow indicators.
evidence_signal: The corrected model is evaluated against an extensive DNS database of Rayleigh-Taylor flows and is reported to improve mixing-layer growth predictions during the transitional regime.
watch_item: The learned closure is validated on Rayleigh-Taylor DNS, so transferability to other turbulent regimes or flow configurations may still require further testing.
paper_title: Learning Turbulence Closures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Rayleigh-Taylor Transition to Turbulence
